vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: amz-hot-keywords
Version: 0.1.1

The skill is a legitimate Amazon keyword scraper that uses Selenium to extract data from the AMZ123 website. The code in scripts/amz_scraper.py aligns perfectly with the documentation in SKILL.md and references/workflow.md, with no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (scraping AMZ123 for hot keywords); it requires local Chrome/Selenium and writes local CSV/JSON files but does not request unrelated credentials or contact unexpected endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim to scrape AMZ123 for ABA-like keyword rankings and the included script implements exactly that: a Selenium-based scraper that navigates to https://www.amz123.com/usatopkeywords, extracts rows, computes trends, and writes CSV/JSON output. The registry metadata declares no env vars or binaries; the SKILL.md and references note prerequisites (Python, Chrome, selenium, pandas) that are reasonable for the stated task. Minor note: the registry did not list Chrome/Selenium as required binaries even though the workflow requires them.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the provided script with CLI flags; the script only accesses the network to load the AMZ123 page, reads the page DOM, and writes a local file. It does not read unrelated system files, environment variables, or send scraped data to external endpoints beyond the target site. Small inconsistency: workflow mentions optional python-dotenv and possible authentication flows but the shipped script does not consume dotenv or other credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec (instruction-only), so nothing is downloaded or written by an installer. The code relies on standard Python packages (selenium, pandas) and a local Chrome binary—this is proportionate to a web-scraping tool and does not use suspicious external download URLs or installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The behavior of the script (headless browser scraping) does not require secrets. The workflow's mention of 'authentication' if ABA becomes gated is a legitimate future extension but is not present in the shipped code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked 'always', and it does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It runs as a one-off scraper and prints the output path. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default, which is expected for skills and not a standalone concern here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: run a local Selenium/Chrome scraper against amz123.com and write a CSV/JSON file. Before installing or running it, ensure you: (1) have Python 3.9+, Chrome, and the listed Python packages installed; (2) run it in an environment where running a headless browser and network access to amz123.com is acceptable; (3) review the code yourself if you are concerned (it prints warnings but does not exfiltrate data); (4) be aware of site terms-of-service and potential bot/CAPTCHA issues—avoid using credentials or storing secrets unless you intentionally extend the script. If you want added safety, run the script in an isolated container or sandbox.
